name: openpixo/starter-platformer
title: Platformer starter
description: Turns a Godot 2D or Phaser template into a side-scrolling platformer with tight jumps, collectibles, enemies and a goal.

useCase.query:
Turn this {{engine.id}} project into a playable side-scrolling platformer. Theme: {{theme}}. Gameplay scope: {{scope}}. Project engine: {{engine.id}}.

Use the existing godot4-2d (Godot 4 2D) or phaser3-vite (Phaser 3) template. Inspect project files first, follow only the matching engine section and its skill, and never migrate engines. If this is a 3D or incompatible project, report that before replacing any scenes.

Requirements:
- Player: gravity, acceleration and friction, variable jump height on early release, 0.1 seconds of coyote time and 0.1 seconds of jump buffering. Map move_left/move_right to arrows and A/D, jump to Space/Up/W. Tune the jump arc so every gap is reachable.
- Keep platforms, collectible positions, checkpoints, hazards and enemy patrol endpoints in level data separate from rendering. Build one level about three screens wide, with solid platforms, a bounded following camera and a visible goal at the far end.
- Falling or touching a hazard respawns at the last checkpoint. Reaching the goal shows Level complete and allows restart. Show collectible count and controls on the HUD. Reset timers, velocity, collectibles and enemies on a full restart.
- Honor the selected scope: patrol enemies can be stomped from above; moving platforms carry the standing player; double jump resets on landing only when requested. Keep these variations in the level/player data.

Engine-specific implementation (use only the matching engine):
- Godot 4 2D / godot4-2d / godot-gdscript: Keep the GL Compatibility renderer, the starter's 1280x720 viewport and its title screen as the entry. Build the game in game/game.tscn and keep its PauseMenu node. Put player-facing text in i18n/strings.csv, and add new rebindable actions to REBINDABLE in autoload/settings.gd. Keep the title screen, settings, pause menu and saves working; a SceneTree check script cannot name their autoloads. Use typed GDScript, focused scene scripts and separate pure model/data scripts. Any written .tscn uses Godot 4 format=3 and correct res:// paths; never edit .godot/. Preserve ui_* input and add named actions for gameplay. Use child Polygon2D/ColorRect shapes and readable Control text as replaceable placeholder visuals. Expose tuning via @export variables or Resources. For CharacterBody2D, velocity is pixels/second and move_and_slide() integrates it; do not multiply velocity by delta again.
- Phaser 3 / phaser3-vite / phaser-game-dev: Keep Phaser 3.90.0, Vite, strict TypeScript and the 800x600 game. Leave src/main.ts as game config, put scenes in src/scenes/, views/objects in src/objects/ and pure rules/data in their own modules. Generate placeholder textures once in BootScene using Graphics.generateTexture; keep texture keys centralized. Preserve src/tuning.ts and src/tuning.json for adjustable values. Use Arcade Physics only when needed; its velocity is pixels/second, while manual movement/timers use delta seconds. Keep the existing pnpm check/build scripts and pinned dependencies; add no new dependencies. Install the declared project dependencies if missing.
- Shared presentation: one consistent palette, clear labels/controls and distinct shapes, with visuals replaceable independently of gameplay. Keep state transitions explicit and clean up timers, tweens and input handlers on restart.

Genre-specific Godot implementation: Rework game/player.gd as CharacterBody2D with move_and_slide() and is_on_floor(). Use StaticBody2D/AnimatableBody2D platforms, Area2D pickups and goal, Camera2D smoothing with limits, and a CanvasLayer HUD.

Genre-specific Phaser implementation: Enable Arcade Physics with world gravity. Use a Player Arcade sprite, static platform bodies and overlap callbacks for pickups/goal. Use body.blocked.down or touching.down for grounded state, an immovable moving platform for that scope, and camera/world bounds wider than the viewport.

Rules checks:
- Coyote-time and buffered-jump boundaries with an injected delta; early release shortens jump height.
- Collecting the same pickup twice counts once; respawn clears velocity and jump timers; restart resets level state.
- Level data places the start/checkpoints/goal on safe surfaces; scoped double jump resets only on landing.

Playtest hints: Use arrows or A/D to move, Space to jump, release Space early to compare jump height, collect a coin, fall and respawn, then reach the goal and restart. Check scoped enemy stomps, moving platforms and double jump. Capture the HUD and a mid-level jump, not only the start screen.

Verification wiring:
- Implement the rules checks above on fresh isolated state with fixed seeds and an injected clock/delta; no real waits, providers or gameplay-state mutations. Phaser: put them in src/checks/rules-check.ts, call them at dev boot before accepting input, and throw on failure so the verify run records an error. Godot: share a reusable check routine between debug boot and a checks/rules_check.gd SceneTree runner; report failures with push_error and exit nonzero. After import, run godot --headless --path . --script checks/rules_check.gd using the configured Godot executable. Verification must exercise these checks, not just typecheck them.
- Finish by running `pixo game verify --steps check,build,run --screenshot --json`. Fix each failing step, then rerun after changes; do not rerun unchanged code. Open the screenshot and confirm playable content and HUD with no errors or blank canvas. Report passed, failed and unavailable steps honestly: a missing Godot executable, export preset/template or capture tool is unavailable, never a pass. Do not manufacture export settings just to silence an unavailable build.
- Follow the playtest hints with actual gameplay input. Use mouse clicks for mouse-driven controls and upgrade/shop menus. If the current playtest adapter cannot inject native Godot input, report that limitation and supply the manual click/key sequence; do not claim the interaction was tested. Record screenshots and any playtest report alongside verification.
